quick.summary: Why nobody reads your detailed design documents and how to fix it.
quick.takeaway: Use bold headings and short bullet points to guide the reader.

beats.line: I wrote a ten page design document. Why did the whole team ignore it?
Imagine a restaurant menu written as one massive paragraph. You would just leave.
True. I just want to find the pasta.
Your team feels the exact same way about massive blocks of text.
They do not read. They scan for what matters to them.
You need to add visual hierarchy.
Can I just say use good headings and bullet points?
Absolutely. Big headings guide the eye. Bullet points break up the text.
So I should chop my huge paragraphs into short lists under bold titles.
Now they will actually read your brilliant design.

quiz.question: You are writing a data architecture doc. What is the best way to format it?
options: Use large text blocks to explain deeply.
Break it up with bold headings and short lists.
Put the whole design into a single table.
Only use diagrams and no text at all.
quiz.explanation: Colleagues scan documents instead of reading them end to end. Headings and bullets help them find the parts they need.

quiz.question: People read engineering documents word for word to fully understand the nuance.
quiz.explanation: No matter how technical the topic, people scan huge blocks of text and often miss the details. Formatting for scanning solves this.
